name: Overly permissive privilege grant
attack_scenario: Attacker steals the app's DB password; because it holds ALL PRIVILEGES ON *.* WITH GRANT OPTION they read every schema, DROP tables, create new superuser-like accounts, and grant themselves persistence across other databases.
negative_test_hint: connect as the application account and run "DROP TABLE users" and assert permission is denied because the account holds only the specific privileges it needs

exemplar.noncompliant: GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON *.* TO 'app'@'%' WITH GRANT OPTION;
exemplar.compliant: GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON app.orders TO 'app'@'10.0.0.5';
exemplar.explanation: OWASP Database Security and CIS benchmarks require least-privilege grants. GRANT ALL, ON *.*, TO PUBLIC, or WITH GRANT OPTION hands an application account (or every account) full DDL/DML plus the ability to re-delegate rights, so a single compromised credential owns the whole server (CWE-732).
